label: early-prefix of d/r/i/0/c-type tokens, then u/2/q/n/k/g/e/p or <DEL>
explanation: Fires only in the encoding half: original steps t=2..7 (mostly 3-5) and the <DEL> step (44% of mass). It almost never fires in the copy phase (0.7% of mass) and never at t=0 or 1. It looks like a content-weighted sum over a short prefix. It is active when the current input is from a group B (u is strongest, then 2, q, n, k, g, e, p, or <DEL>) and nearly all earlier inputs come from a group A (d, r, i strongest, then 0, c, x, y, a, s). It fires almost only on the first occurrence of the current token (in_first). Magnitude is largest for short prefixes made of d/i/r, e.g. d d f <DEL>, i r d u, d i c <DEL>, and falls off as t and L grow, since more non-A tokens dilute the prefix. By itself <DEL> is weak (precision 5%). The rule is graded rather than crisp, so precision stays around 0.3.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the input two steps back (most: d, r, i, 0, c, s; least: u, n, k, -) and the current input token, by phase (input phase: u, 2, n, q; copy phase: u, k, q, 2; delimiter step: <DEL>); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, t=3, t=4.
